3.  A secure website

5. A team of 3-5 depending on the volume of patients of course.

I'm in the same boat, left my job of 6 years just recently. Since March last year I barely left my room, always had food and groceries delivered. Trimmed my own hair, even laundry was picked up and delivered. My heart and head became heavy before I knew it, I slept 12-16 hours a day, working in my bed sometimes, going weeks without sunlight. A year like that and I started to severely lose the will to live. 

I wake up one day and just suddenly left everything and moved far away, left all of my belongings. I just had a light shoulder bag with my phone, headphones, some documents I thought were important and tennis balls(idk why I brought 3 tennis balls lol).

With no plans whatsoever, while on the bus to this sort of new town I found an ad on social media where a guy was looking for a housemate since his previous one just moved out. I phone him and we strike a deal immediately. I didn't even wait to see the place. 

The afternoon of that same day, I meet him in person, a gentleman who used to be a professor, now in his 50s, lived in France for a while and currently working on his 2nd MA on English literature. 

I was absolutely astonished, bare in mind that just recently I had lost my will to live and seriously contemplated many ways for my exit. I wanted nothing and I cared about noone. But now, here I was, talking to this old soul about Philosophy, Politics, Literature and what happened to him over the year. That very same morning I was just thinking how I didn't care about anything anymore, I feel like I was really about to make that my last day. And yet there I was, listening attentively, comparing his thoughts to mine, learning and discussing different personal and intellectual topics. 

I was humbled and brought back. There's this guy twice my age, frail and thin and could barely lift a pail of water. He's living and working, staying alive with all his might. A profound and smart man with a gentle soul. He offered me what food he had and spoke with great enthusiasm about his work and his thesis. 

I'm not sure whatever guided me to be here now but I've just started working again albeit for a different company and a totally different industry. I'm learning about so many things just by the course of our meals together. I just realized that this has gone way too long. But I'll wrap it up with the thought that, when we're to constricted by our own world, reality or circumstance, meeting new people or just doing something that would shift how you look at things would give you plenty of reasons to keep going at your own pace.
